statusDetail: The homepage was inspected across visual, responsive, accessibility, performance, network, security, crawler, and memory conditions, but the representative search-results journey redirected to Google’s unusual-traffic reCAPTCHA. One atomic check is blocked, so this 57/58 run is partial and has no score.

paths.description: Google Search homepage: landing template, consent state, search control, preferences, responsive behavior, accessibility, performance, security, and memory.
Primary journey from a query to the search-results archetype. Direct navigation was attempted and redirected to unusual-traffic reCAPTCHA.
Raw HTML/no-JavaScript crawler view paired with the rendered homepage.

findings.summary: The page stays dark even when the browser explicitly requests a light color scheme.
findings.evidence: Evaluate probes under prefers-color-scheme: light and dark both returned body background rgb(34, 36, 42) and text rgb(232, 232, 232); the light and dark screenshots are byte-identical.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the chosen palette follow prefers-color-scheme by default, declare color-scheme, and reserve any manual theme override for an explicit user choice.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the primary search experience on initial load.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot shows a modal covering nearly the full viewport before interaction; the DOM probe identifies an aria-modal=true consent dialog over the search form.
findings.suggestedFix: Where legally permissible, use a compact, content-preserving consent surface. If a modal is required, keep the essential explanation concise and make dismissal/choice immediate and keyboard-safe.

findings.summary: The active consent modal is implemented as a div with ARIA rather than the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM/evaluate probe reports the visible consent surface as DIV role=dialog aria-modal=true, while the only native DIALOG belongs to a separate hidden voice-search surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> for the modal consent flow with declarative close behavior and correct initial/return focus, retaining ARIA only where native semantics need augmentation.

findings.summary: The desktop document is scaled down rather than genuinely reflowing at a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout capture reports no viewport meta and a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport scaled to about 0.367 inside a 360px device viewport; the full-page screenshot shows tiny desktop navigation and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a standards-based viewport meta tag and use fluid/intrinsic layout so content reflows at narrow widths rather than relying on browser shrink-to-fit.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus on the primary search field has no visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: After focusing the search textarea, the evaluate probe returned outline "none" and box-shadow "none"; several visible search buttons are only 36 CSS pixels high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator to the search control and keep interactive targets at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels where practical.

findings.summary: The primary keyboard focus state is not visually perceivable.
findings.evidence: The focused search textarea is the activeElement but its computed outline is none and box-shadow is none. The generic first focusable link probe also returned no outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an unmistakable :focus-visible ring for every interactive element, including the search field and header/footer links, without removing the browser outline unless an equivalent is supplied.

findings.summary: The simple search landing page ships a disproportionately large JavaScript payload with measurable unused code.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary reports 703,019 transferred script bytes out of 803,606 total bytes. Lighthouse flags both unused JavaScript and unused CSS, each at score 0.5.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and conditionally load nonessential modules after user intent, remove duplicate/unused bundles, and keep the initial search shell to the code needed for search and consent.

findings.summary: At least one text link relies on color alone to be distinguishable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse link-in-text-block failed with one affected item, while the separate color-contrast audit passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a non-color affordance such as an underline for inline links, with clear hover and focus states.

findings.summary: The narrow-viewport experience uses shrink-to-fit instead of accessible reflow.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout metrics expose a 980px CSS layout viewport and no viewport meta, producing a 0.367 visual scale and very small desktop text and links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a responsive viewport declaration and reflow the page at narrow widths while preserving user zoom and adequate target sizes.

findings.summary: The public homepage has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe returned description=null and Lighthouse failed the meta-description audit. The title is present as "Google".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, locale-appropriate meta description that explains Google Search and matches visible page intent.

findings.summary: The homepage redirect target does not expose an explicit canonical URL.
findings.evidence: https://google.com/ redirects to https://www.google.com/, but the rendered DOM probe reports canonical=null. robots.txt is valid and the document returns 200 after the redirect.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit self-referencing canonical for the final locale-aware homepage URL, or document the intentional canonicalization policy through stable redirects and locale signals.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes no structured entity or social-preview metadata in the inspected DOM.
findings.evidence: The DOM/evaluate evidence contains no JSON-LD, Open Graph metadata, or equivalent structured description for the Google Search/Organization entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish accurate Organization/WebSite structured data and basic share-preview metadata that reflects the visible search homepage.

findings.summary: The inspected main document omits several baseline security response headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, but reports missing Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a deliberate Referrer-Policy on the final www.google.com document.

findings.summary: The page performs background logging and async-data requests before the user resolves the consent modal.
findings.evidence: The initial-load HAR includes play.google.com/log requests and requests to ogads-pa.clients6.google.com while the screenshot still shows the unresolved consent dialog. The tracker matcher found no known tracker domain, so the classification is medium-confidence rather than asserting ad tracking.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit every pre-consent request, document its necessity, and defer nonessential logging/analytics until a valid user choice; batch any permitted telemetry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The headers capture finds clickjacking protection and Permissions-Policy unload=(), but no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors policy, Referrer-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), set nosniff and a deliberate Referrer-Policy, and expand Permissions-Policy to the minimum capabilities needed.

findings.summary: Initial resource use is heavy for a single-field search landing page.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 43 requests and 803,606 transferred bytes, including 703,019 bytes of JavaScript; Lighthouse separately identifies unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an initial-load budget for the search shell, conditionally fetch optional modules, and deprioritize or defer background data and telemetry.

findings.summary: The core search form is not exposed as a structured agent capability.
findings.evidence: The evaluate probe reports navigator.modelContext absent and no agentic form/tool annotations, despite search being a clear, bounded capability suitable for structured invocation.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider exposing the search form through declarative WebMCP/agentic-form metadata with explicit descriptions, input constraints, and safe user confirmation semantics.

findings.summary: The homepage omits viewport metadata and is shrink-to-fit rather than mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout metrics report hasViewportMeta=false, a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport, and visual scale 0.367; the mobile screenshot shows very small desktop UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 viewport metadata and use fluid layout rules so controls and text render at usable mobile sizes.
